newsitem.title: UK: HK in London up, HSBC rises on broker comment.
newsitem.headline: HK in London up, HSBC rises on broker comment.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks in London were mostly firmer on Tuesday, dragged higher by a strong performance from heavyweight banking group HSBC Holdings, dealers said.

Shares in HSBC gained HK$5.12-1/2 to close at HK$259.12-1/2 after brokerage Dresdner Kleinwort Benson raised its price target for the banking group's ordinary shares to 24.00 stg from 21.00 stg. HSBC is due to report its half-year results on August 4.

The Hang Seng London Reference Index rose 11.39 points to finish at 15,498.63, following the second consecutive record-breaking session in Hong Kong. On Tuesday, the Hang Seng Index climbed 116.30 points to an all-time closing high of 15,487.24.

Elsewhere, dealers said property issues remained around their Hong Kong closing levels after the Hong Kong government on Tuesday approved arrangements which allow for the granting of new land leases and extension of existing leases beyond the year 2047.
The arrangements preserve the British system whereby all land in Hong Kong is considered to be held by the government, which sells or grants leaseholds at its discretion.
